issues.detail: 'NOT id IN (...)' is valid PostgreSQL syntax and behaves like NOT IN; calling it invalid is incorrect.

corrections.from: Option C has the same NULL sensitivity, and option D is not valid PostgreSQL syntax.
corrections.to: Option C has the same NULL sensitivity, and option D applies NOT to the same IN test, so it is also NULL-sensitive and returns no rows when the subquery yields NULL.
corrections.reason: The option is syntactically valid; its defect is NULL semantics, not syntax.

citations.quote: Note that if the left-hand expression yields null, or if there are no equal right-hand values and at least one right-hand row yields null, the result of the NOT IN construct will be null, not true.
NOT IN is equivalent to <> ALL .

questions.notes: NOT EXISTS is the reliable NULL-safe anti-join and is the correct answer. The explanation's final claim that option D is invalid syntax is wrong: 'NOT id IN (subquery)' parses in PostgreSQL 17 and is semantically the same NULL-sensitive NOT IN, so it also returns no rows when the subquery yields NULL. Verified by execution on PostgreSQL 17.11.
